summary:
Amazonia Guardian is a web application developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge of Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots.

The project allows users to import hotspot datasets in CSV format, process and visualize fire detection information, and compare data from MODIS and VIIRS satellites. Its goal is to make satellite hotspot information easier to access, understand, and analyze.

By combining data from these two satellite sources, Amazonia Guardian aims to support the identification and monitoring of potential forest fire events in the Amazon rainforest.

This project highlights the importance of Earth observation data and accessible technology in environmental monitoring, helping people better understand fire activity and promoting awareness about protecting the Amazon ecosystem.
details:
Project Details – Amazonia Guardian

Amazonia Guardian is a web application designed to make satellite hotspot information easier to access, process, visualize, and understand. It addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026: Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots.

How does it work?

The application allows users to import hotspot datasets in CSV format. It processes the information and presents the detected hotspots through a user-friendly interface, helping users explore and compare information from MODIS and VIIRS satellite observations.

Benefits and expected impact

Amazonia Guardian aims to support environmental monitoring by making satellite fire detection data more accessible and understandable. It can help users identify potential fire activity, explore hotspot patterns, and improve awareness of forest fire risks in the Amazon rainforest.

Its expected impact is to promote the use of Earth observation data for environmental protection and encourage informed decisions about forest conservation.

Technologies and tools

The project was developed using:

  • Python for data processing and application logic.
  • HTML and CSS for the user interface.
  • JavaScript for interactive functionality.
  • CSV files for importing satellite hotspot datasets.
  • Git and GitHub for version control and project management.

Creativity and innovation

The creative aspect of Amazonia Guardian is its focus on bringing MODIS and VIIRS hotspot information together in an accessible web application. Instead of requiring users to work directly with complex satellite datasets, the platform provides a simpler way to explore and understand the information.

Design considerations

The project considers data accessibility, usability, clarity of visualization, and the importance of environmental monitoring. It is designed as an initial technological solution that can be expanded with additional satellite datasets, analytical tools, and geospatial capabilities.

Amazonia Guardian aims to connect technology, satellite data, and environmental awareness to contribute to the protection of the Amazon.
